chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who completed his Hajj, then turned back, and when he had exited the Haram, a prey faced him near the Haram, and the prey was heading towards the Haram. So he shot at it and killed it. What is upon him regarding that? He said: He ransoms it in the same manner.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for killing game after completing Hajj and exiting Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the transitional legal status of a pilgrim who has completed the core rites of Hajj and released from Ihram but remains within the sacred precincts (Haram). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if game is killed near the boundary while the animal is moving toward the Haram, the pilgrim must still pay fidyah, demonstrating that the sanctity of the space extends the duration of the hunting prohibition even after the formal rites are concluded. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual boundaries and the specific conditions under which the state of Ihram's restrictions persist.
